_README: Edge-Function deploy ledger (B-178 / CUL-135). One entry per deployable function. `fingerprint` = the sha256 of the function's shipping import-closure (index.ts + every local .ts it inlines) last acknowledged for deploy — computed by guards/edgeFunctionDeploy.test.ts, which FAILS THE BUILD when a function drifts from its recorded fingerprint without a reasoned acknowledgment. Statuses: `deployed` (fingerprint confirmed live), `pending` (a deploy is owed OR the live state is unverified — see the entry's `reason`), `hold` (deliberately not deployed — e.g. B-494). `pending`/`hold` require a `reason`. After deploying a function, set its `fingerprint` to the current value (the guard's failure message prints it) with status `deployed`. This ledger records intent; it does NOT prove a deploy happened — see docs/edge-deploy-runbook.md § Deploy ledger.
_seed: Seeded 2026-08-19 (CUL-135). Fingerprints are the current main closures at ledger creation. Live-vs-main was NOT verified per-function (the live artifact is a bundle, not a source closure, and this guard is token-free by design), so no function is seeded `deployed`: generate-report is the one confirmed `hold` (B-494); every other function is `pending` (baseline). Each converts to `deployed` on its next verified deploy-from-main, or via the live reconciliation follow-on (CUL-541).

generate-report.reason: B-494 HOLD UNCHANGED — CUL-19 still gates this function; nothing in W1-PR-3b session 2 relaxes it, and this re-acknowledgment must not be read as progress toward clearing it. Fingerprint re-bumped for CUL-676's report co-work (§10.5 / HR-3 — a lane-membership change IS report work): `cough` + `sneeze` joined REPORT_SYMPTOM_TYPES (cough HAD to, because buildDetectionInput filters on CORRELATION_SYMPTOM_TYPES, so the report now runs ⑦ over cough and would otherwise print a chronicity flag about a sign its own §3.5 table never counts — the B-494 class); render.ts gained proper 'Coughing'/'Sneezing' labels; the report's `chronicity` extract became a LIST so R4's second course is not silently discarded; HR-7 was applied — §3.5 is relabelled 'entries' (it counts minute-deduped rows) while the chronicity flag keeps 'episodes' (3h-chained), with a new legend entry explaining that the two differ on purpose. It also inlines generate-signal/detection.ts, so every engine change above rides this fingerprint. Prior hold notes (CUL-564 §3.8 timing render, CUL-372 episode-collapse re-base) remain in force. Do NOT set `deployed` until B-494 clears. RE-FINGERPRINTED after the adversarial pass (2026-08-28): two further HR-7 residuals fixed (the page-1 tile said 'Episodes' over the trendHalves ENTRIES count, disagreeing with the trend panel's own noun on the same page — the B-532 divergence class; and the days-since tile's noun), plus a genuine unit bug the pass found — `episodeSetMatches` compared minute-deduped ROWS against the engine's 3h-CHAINED episode count, so for every cough flag the local-day reconciliation of symptomDays/daysSinceLastEpisode silently disabled itself and fell back to UTC numbers beside a local-day tile, reinstating the ±1-day disagreement the PR-7 cold read caught on the lead safety line. It now chains the report's rows with the shared lib/symptomEpisodes predicate and compares like for like. B-494/CUL-19 hold UNCHANGED. Re-fingerprinted again for the R3 re-ruling (it inlines detection.ts, so the gate split rides this closure). B-494/CUL-19 hold UNCHANGED. Also carries the CUL-687 verification fix: the chronicity flag's BOLD LEAD said 'has been ongoing 28 days' in the same sentence as 'most recent 27 days ago' — reachable once cough's recency floor widened, and a self-contradiction on the line the legend teaches a vet to scan first. Now 'spans N days'; recency keeps its own clause. B-494/CUL-19 hold UNCHANGED. RE-FINGERPRINTED for CUL-69/B-700 — the chronicity flag's onset date. It printed `firstOnsetIso` as "(first logged {date})", but that field is bounded by the DETECTOR's own lookback (a single global 56d for every symptom type — `chronicity.perType` overrides the FLOORS only, never the lookback), while the report's default window is the 90-day fallback — buildDetectionInput's contract states the containment ("90-day fallback ⊃ 56d chronicity window") and that containment IS the defect: for any course predating the lookback the onset lands ~34 days inside the window, so the lead safety line dated a cat vomiting since May 20 as "first logged Jun 13" while appendix A on the same report printed May 20. Three weeks short, contradicting the report's own log, on the axis a vet reads a chronicity flag FOR — and understating duration is the reassuring direction, which is the one direction this band may not fail in (B-494). B-532's left-censor did not catch it: it tested the onset against the REPORT window edge, the boundary that is not binding here. The flag now carries `firstLoggedIso` (the earliest in-window entry of that symptom, the same rows appendix A prints) beside `firstOnsetIso`, the exposureRange-vs-range split; the rendered date and span anchor to it, the censor floor tests it, and the engine's counts are UNCHANGED but now disclose their own window rather than being re-derived (the C5 disclosure precedent — re-deriving would fork the report off the one statistical source and make this flag disagree with the Signal card for the same pet). RE-FINGERPRINTED after the adversarial pass returned FAIL on the first draft (2026-08-30). The draft also EXTENDED the span by the record preceding the lookback, so the two numbers would agree — and that re-opened §10 #4, the "two distant data points" break the engine closes with `loggingEligible` over both halves of the span, `countDistributionWeeks`' B-188 anti-barbell packing, and the minSpan/minEpisodes conjunction. One stale vomit ten months before a real six-week course printed "spans 335 days · 7 episodes": the duration ran toward alarm and was false, while the DENSITY a vet triages on ran toward reassurance — one episode every seven weeks over a record holding weekly vomiting, which is the B-494 direction. Cough was the worst case, its 28-day recency floor letting a long-quiet course fire and maximising the gap, and the left-censor then restated the manufactured number as an affirmative clinical minimum ("348 days is a floor"). The generalisable rule, now written into render.ts: A RECORD-ANCHORED DATE IS A FACT AND FREE TO STATE; A DURATION IS AN INFERENCE THE ENGINE GUARDS, and any layer that widens it inherits those guards or must not widen it. So the span stays `f.spanDays`, the date comes from `firstLoggedIso`, and where the record reaches back past the counts the two are stated in separate sentences (the "spans N days (first logged X)" parenthetical drops, since glued to the span it asserts a duration nobody measured). Two further pass findings fixed with it: the disclosure now names the DATE the counts begin at rather than the lookback LENGTH (which runs back from the window end, so "the most recent 56 days of that span" could exceed a 43-day span and read as "nothing is missing" — the inverse of the warning), and its gate is INSTANT-granular rather than day-granular (the lookback cuts at an instant, so three morning episodes sat uncounted and undisclosed behind a same-local-day comparison). What the pass confirmed HELD: span-shrink is impossible (clamped, and the anchor ordering is structural), the new censor predicate is implied by the old one so it can only fire more often, the `min` is inert by construction across dedup/3h-chaining/custom windows (0/201 fuzzed flags), the mixed-unit arithmetic does not compound (±1 day, identical to main), and flag-vs-appendix-A disagreement falls from 60 days to 1 across a 219-flag fuzz over seven timezones. RE-FINGERPRINTED AGAIN after a SECOND adversarial pass on the corrected version (2026-08-30), which confirmed the span/date split holds (351 fuzzed flags across 7 timezones: the rendered span equals `f.spanDays` every time, and the flag's date equals appendix A's earliest row of that type every time — 0 days of disagreement, against up to 60 on main) and then broke three more things in the two SENTENCES AROUND it. (1) The left-censor stated the ENGINE span as the clinical floor in a paragraph that had just cited an earlier record anchor, understating the floor by a median 32 days over dense chronic records (max 62) — the reassuring direction, and newly reachable because the censor was effectively dead on the old anchor. Fixed by splitting on which boundary actually binds: the two cases are disjoint by construction (`hasUncountedRecord` entails window > lookback), so where only the window truncates, B-532's sentence is unchanged and correct; where BOTH truncate, no single number is defensible — `f.spanDays` understates and the record's own extent is two logged rows rather than a measured course (that direction is the first pass's finding 1 arriving through the censor) — so the window fact is stated with no duration attached. (2) The instant-granular gate from pass 1 could print one date twice ("was first logged May 7; these counts begin at May 7") on ~5% of boundary-edge cough flags, because the gate is an instant while both rendered dates are local days; the same-local-day case now reads "these counts begin later that day". (3) The disclosure introduced a second analysis window with no legend entry, against the HR-7 precedent, leaving the reassuring inference (that the engine judged the earlier entries unrelated) available — there is now a gated "Where the chronicity counts begin" entry that closes it in as many words, gated like the incident-photos entry so it never explains a line the report does not carry (B-599). The tail copy is also number-agnostic, since this layer does not hold the count it was pluralising over. Both defect-pinning tests were rewritten: the censor test had asserted the floor may never be tighter than the span, and the instant-granular test's own fixture WAS the same-date sentence while asserting only that the disclosure fired. Every guard mutation-proved (CUL-613). B-494/CUL-19 hold UNCHANGED; this re-acknowledgment is not progress toward clearing it.
